content.overview: BNS s. 13 — Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction. BNS restatement of IPC 75. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 75. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 13 is the rule on “Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction”. The section provides that whoever, having been convicted by a Court in India, of an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII of this Sanhita with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards, shall be guilty of any offence punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term, shall be subject for every such subsequent offence to imprisonment for life, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 13 exists so that “Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction” has a closed legal test in Chapter II — Of Punishments. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Death, life, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service. How sentences combine, commute and enhance.

The provision in detail
13. Whoever, having been convicted by a Court in India, of an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII of this Sanhita with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards, shall be guilty of any offence punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term, shall be subject for every such subsequent offence to imprisonment for life, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years

CHAPTER III - GENERAL EXCEPTIONS

GENERAL EXCEPTIONS

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, having been convicted by a Court in India, of an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII of this Sanhita with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards, shall be guilty of any offence punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term, shall be subject for every such subsequent offence to imprisonment for life, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years
2. CHAPTER III - GENERAL EXCEPTIONS

learningObjectives: Identify the previous-conviction condition in BNS s.13.
Limit the section to later offences under Chapter X or Chapter XVII with the stated imprisonment threshold.
State the enhanced punishment without treating it as a new offence.
enhancement.definition: BNS s.13 subjects a person to imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description up to ten years, for a later qualifying offence after a qualifying conviction in India under Chapter X or Chapter XVII.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 13 is an enhanced-punishment rule for a subsequent offence. It does not convict the person of the earlier offence again, and it applies only where both the previous conviction and the later offence meet the Chapter and imprisonment conditions.
statutoryFramework: BNS s.13, placed with punishments; general exceptions begin at s.14.
Previous conviction by a court in India.
That conviction must be for an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII with imprisonment of either description for three years or upwards.
The later offence must also be punishable under either of those Chapters with like imprisonment for the like term.
For every such subsequent offence the person is subject to imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years.
essentialIngredients: A previous conviction by a court in India.
The previous offence is punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII with imprisonment of either description for a term of three years or upwards.
A later offence punishable under either of those Chapters with imprisonment of either description for three years or upwards.
The enhanced liability is for that subsequent offence.
The stated punishment is imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description extending to ten years.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 13 is the successor heading to the old enhanced-punishment rule for repeat offending in the coin/currency and property chapters. Both ends of the sequence matter. The earlier conviction must be by a court in India and must be for an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII with imprisonment of either description for three years or upwards. The new offence must be punishable under either of those Chapters with the same imprisonment threshold. A previous conviction outside those Chapters, or for an offence whose punishment is below three years, does not trigger s.13. The section then makes the person liable, for every such subsequent offence, to imprisonment for life or to imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years. It is a punishment consequence, not a definition of theft, cheating or a coin offence. The migrated study note in this file also prints a Chapter III heading; that heading belongs to the general exceptions, which start at s.14. Do not treat s.13 itself as a general exception.
examples: Teaching example: a person was earlier convicted in India of a Chapter XVII offence punishable with three years or more, and is later convicted of another Chapter XVII offence punishable with three years or more. Section 13 can be considered for the later offence.
Teaching example: the earlier conviction was for an offence punishable with a maximum of one year. The three-year threshold fails, so s.13 does not apply.
Teaching example: both offences are outside Chapter X and Chapter XVII. Section 13 is not the enhancement route.
distinctions: Section 13 enhances punishment for a subsequent qualifying offence. It is not a general exception and does not excuse the later act.
The previous conviction must be by a court in India. A foreign conviction is not what the section states.
Ordinary punishment in the offence section still has to be identified; s.13 is an additional liability rule where its conditions are proved.
problemApplication: Issue: whether the later conviction attracts enhanced punishment under s.13.
Rule: previous Indian conviction and later offence, each punishable under Chapter X or XVII with imprisonment of either description for three years or upwards.
Application: name the chapter and the imprisonment threshold for each offence. If either fails, stop.
Conclusion: if both qualify, the person is subject to imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description up to ten years for the subsequent offence.

shortAnswer: State the previous-conviction and same-chapter conditions.
State life imprisonment or imprisonment up to ten years for the subsequent offence.
tenMark: Introduction: enhanced punishment, not a new offence.
Previous conviction by a court in India.
Chapter X or XVII and the three-year threshold, applied twice.
One failure example and a conclusion.
sixteenMark: Why both the earlier and later offences must qualify.
Distinction from general exceptions in ss.14-15.
Distinction from ordinary sentence and from solitary confinement.

keyTakeaways: Both the previous conviction and the later offence must fall in Chapter X or Chapter XVII.
Each must be punishable with imprisonment of either description for three years or upwards.
The enhancement is for the subsequent offence: life, or imprisonment up to ten years.
